name: github-workflow
description: Community plugin for GitHub-based development workflows. Say 'start the next story' and the plugin picks an issue from your backlog, plans the architecture, builds it, runs tests, opens a PR, has that PR reviewed independently by agents in a fresh context, and applies the fixes the review asks for. It merges the PR too on projects that turn on auto-merge, which is one setting governing every command that can merge. Selection is structured rather than textual: Stage, Priority, Effort and Ownership are org issue fields, so a run never reads a label, a board card or an issue body to decide anything. An issue carries its own state, so it is pickable whether or not anybody added it to a board, and every board that groups by Stage shows the same answer. A scheduled `board-sync` workflow adds any board card GitHub's auto-add missed and keeps every issue's Stage in step with its real state, moving work owned by a person or a browser agent to `Non-code` and filing an issue with no Stage in `Backlog`. It reads the Epic and Feature tree too: an Epic or Feature can be picked and expands to the stories under it, parking one sets aside everything beneath it, a bulk run can take its set from the stories under one Epic or Feature, and an Epic or Feature is closed once its last sub-issue closes. An issue too unclear to build is sent to refinement rather than guessed at. Every interview, from stress-testing a plan to scoping a feature, runs through one shared `grill` skill, which leads each question with a recommendation and never guesses an answer when nobody is there to give it. Supports sprint-based and flat backlogs. Bundles skills, commands and agents with least-privilege tool access, plus a setup wizard that auto-detects your project configuration and a preflight check that repairs what it safely can.
